principles: Preserve gate authority: reviewer evidence remains reviewer-written and signed.
Fix only the real user-facing confusion, not broader lifecycle behavior.
Keep local CLI guidance separate from Authority Server proof.
Make execution reproducible through Lattice lifecycle artifacts.
drivers: PLAN review blockers must be actionable without implying a missing command.
The execution document must be auditable before implementation.
High-risk lifecycle changes need clear rollback and verification.

options.name: A: Write audited execution plan first, then hand implementation to Lattice
pros: Matches the user request for plan + two-host audit before execution
Avoids changing gate behavior before the correctness boundary is agreed
Keeps implementation scope narrow and testable
cons: Adds one lifecycle story before code changes
Requires a second execution step after the document is finalized

options.name: B: Directly implement better missing_scope_check hints now
cons: Skips the requested audited plan document
Risks changing the wrong surface because story_review already has some guidance

options.name: C: Auto-generate scope-check evidence when missing
pros: Would remove a manual step for users
cons: Confuses main-agent execution with signed scope reviewer evidence
Violates the real gate semantics and should be rejected

chosen: A: Write audited execution plan first, then hand implementation to Lattice
rationale: Choose the audited execution plan first because this is a high-risk lifecycle ergonomics change and the existing command already exists; the real issue is consistency and actionability of guidance, not missing functionality.

preMortem.scenario: The plan accidentally weakens PLAN review by recommending auto-created scope-check evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Trying to make missing_scope_check disappear automatically.
preMortem.consequence: Main agent could self-absolve scope review and reduce gate integrity.
preMortem.mitigation: State that scope_check_save remains reviewer-written signed evidence; implementation may only improve guidance.

preMortem.scenario: The plan overclaims Authority Server involvement.
preMortem.trigger: Treating local Lattice CLI guidance as receipt-backed proof.
preMortem.consequence: Users think Authority completion was verified when only local docs/hints changed.
preMortem.mitigation: Add explicit Non-authority/Authority boundary and no Authority Server completion claim.

preMortem.scenario: The implementation target is too broad and becomes arbitrary optimization.
preMortem.trigger: Expanding from one blocker message to a general lifecycle assistant rewrite.
preMortem.consequence: Higher regression risk and inconsistent logic across gates.
preMortem.mitigation: Limit execution to missing_scope_check actionability and consistency across existing surfaces only.
